beats.headline: Stocks closed a losing week as Mideast tensions and AI-spending jitters weighed on shares
beats.body: For the week ending July 24, the S&P 500 fell about 0.5%, the Nasdaq 0.8%, and the Dow 0.2% as oil prices rose on renewed US-Iran hostilities and investors balked at huge AI capital-spending plans from Alphabet and Tesla; Intel shares dropped nearly 8% even after beating earnings estimates.

beats.headline: Shots fired at the US consulate in Toronto for the second time this year
beats.body: A gunman fired at least one round at the US consulate in downtown Toronto early Monday morning, damaging the building's facade but causing no injuries; police pursued a fleeing sedan and are investigating a possible link to gun-for-hire networks tied to earlier attacks, including a March shooting at the same building.

beats.headline: Carrier strike group patrols South China Sea after Philippine-Chinese clashes
beats.body: The USS George Washington and its strike group are conducting the Navy's only forward-deployed carrier's first patrol of 2026 in the South China Sea, following days of clashes in which Chinese coast guard vessels fired water cannon at Philippine government ships near Scarborough Shoal on July 23-24.

beats.headline: US enforces Iran naval blockade, boarding and disabling tankers in the Arabian Sea
beats.body: CENTCOM says it has redirected 12 commercial vessels, disabled two that refused to comply, and boarded two more for verification since reimposing a naval blockade on Iran, including a boarding of the tanker M/T Charminar and disabling of the tanker M/T Lavine in the Gulf of Oman on July 24.

beats.headline: Pentagon seeks cheap, fast-to-field long-range strike drones
beats.body: The Pentagon issued a call for autonomously guided 'Ground-Based Affordable Mass' munitions costing under $250,000 each, asking industry to have prototypes ready for demonstration within three months as the military pushes to field large numbers of low-cost long-range strike weapons quickly.

beats.headline: Private Claude conversations turned up in Google search results
beats.body: Anthropic is responding to a privacy lapse after users discovered that chats shared via Claude's 'share' feature, some containing sensitive data like crypto wallet keys, had been indexed and surfaced in public Google search results. The incident follows Anthropic's July 24 release of Claude Opus 5, its fourth Claude 5-family model in under two months, which matches or beats Fable 5 on many benchmarks at roughly half the price.

beats.headline: Bears open camp with Kyler Gordon and T.J. Edwards on injury lists
beats.body: Chicago placed cornerback Kyler Gordon on the active/PUP list with a lingering soft-tissue injury and linebacker T.J. Edwards on active/NFI with a reported minor muscle strain, among six players sidelined as training camp opens at Halas Hall for coach Ben Johnson's second season after last year's 11-win, NFC North title run.

beats.headline: No fresh news on this beat right now
beats.body: The most recent Cup Series race, the Brickyard 400 on July 26, falls inside the seven-day spoiler window, and no roster, injury, schedule, or sponsorship news independent of race results surfaced in the past few days.

beats.headline: Valparaiso schools superintendent's resignation takes effect this month
beats.body: Jim McCall's resignation as Valparaiso Community Schools superintendent, announced in April after 27 years with the district, takes effect this month as he moves to the private sector. Separately, Duneland School Corporation's phone-free policy for students, required under Indiana's new bell-to-bell cellphone law, has been in effect since July 1.

beats.headline: PCA mourns longtime Old Testament scholar Robert Vasholz, who died July 16
beats.body: Dr. Robert I. Vasholz, professor emeritus of Old Testament at Covenant Theological Seminary in St. Louis, died July 16 at age 90 after more than three decades teaching Hebrew and Semitic languages at the PCA's flagship seminary; his memorial service was held July 24 at Redeemer Presbyterian Church.
